item.title: M&S Brings Sustainable Sprouts to Christmas Tables With Seed to Shelf Farming
item.description: From wildflower planting to hand trimmed produce, a Scottish farm near Arbroath is shaping how M&S grows its Christmas Brussels sprouts, blending biodiversity, climate conscious farming, and long term partnerships to deliver better food while protecting nature.The post M&S Brings Sustainable Sprouts to Christmas Tables With Seed to Shelf Farming appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: No Cheer Keir Puts Premium on Price of Your Pint
item.description: Pubs across Scotland are warning of higher pint prices and potential job cuts after new budget pressures, with industry leaders and SNP politicians urging action to protect local hospitality venues during the Christmas period.The post No Cheer Keir Puts Premium on Price of Your Pint appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Bah Humbug as One in Five Brits Talk to Their Car to Cope With Christmas Chaos
item.description: As Christmas pressure builds, new research shows one in five UK drivers talk to their car to cope with festive stress, highlighting how winter travel, busy roads, and packed schedules turn vehicles into trusted companions during the most chaotic time of year.The post Bah Humbug as One in Five Brits Talk to Their Car to Cope With Christmas Chaos appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Eat Safe Award Presented to Engebret Ltd in Stornoway
item.description: A Stornoway food business has been recognised for exceptional hygiene standards after Engebret Ltd received a Food Standards Scotland Eat Safe Award, highlighting the role of local Environmental Health teams in supporting food safety and helping customers choose where to eat with confidence. The post Eat Safe Award Presented to Engebret Ltd in Stornoway appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Council Receives Top Award for Catch The Bus Month 2025 Campaign
item.description: The Highland Council has been recognised with a national award for its Catch the Bus Month 2025 campaign, highlighting efforts to promote public transport, connect communities, and encourage more people across the Highlands to choose bus travel for everyday journeys.The post Council Receives Top Award for Catch The Bus Month 2025 Campaign appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Highlands’ Own Oasis Tribute Band to Launch at An Seomar With a Touch Of Mystery
item.description: A new Highland Oasis tribute band will make its live debut at An Seomar in Inverness on 30 December, with no photos released and the full reveal saved for the night itself, blending local music talent, classic anthems, and support for mental health charities.The post Highlands’ Own Oasis Tribute Band to Launch at An Seomar With a Touch Of Mystery appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Get The Right Care at The Right Place This Festive Season
item.description: Scots are being urged to check NHS inform before calling 111 or 999 this festive season, as rising winter demand puts pressure on health services and emergency care, with clear guidance aimed at helping people get the right care in the right place.The post Get The Right Care at The Right Place This Festive Season appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Council Staff Dig Deep to Support Highland Hospice
item.description: Staff from The Highland Council have raised £1,640 for Highland Hospice through a festive bake sale and charity raffle, highlighting the generosity of council teams and their continued support for vital hospice care across the Highlands.The post Council Staff Dig Deep to Support Highland Hospice appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: All I Want For Christmas is This Ducati
item.description: Ducati has unveiled the Panigale V4 Márquez 2025 World Champion Replica, a 293 unit collector superbike celebrating MotoGP glory, factory pride, and cutting edge racing technology, in a Christmas season reveal that blends motorsport success with pure two wheeled desire.The post All I Want For Christmas is This Ducati appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Shoppers Hit With £71 Million in Delivery Surcharges This Year
item.description: Households in the Highlands and Islands have paid an estimated £71 million in delivery surcharges this year, with new figures prompting calls for the UK Government to step in and end extra costs that campaigners say unfairly penalise rural shoppers, particularly at Christmas. The post Shoppers Hit With £71 Million in Delivery Surcharges This Year appeared first on The Highland Times.
